proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(P_S=\operatorname{diag}_{a\in S}(L_\pi^{(a)})\), with the blocks ordered by view.  Every \(\Sigma^{aa}\) is positive definite: under \(\text{def:component-aligned-limvam-class}\), \(X^{(a)}=(I_p-B^{0,(a)})^{-1}\varepsilon^{(a)}\), the matrix \(I_p-B^{0,(a)}\) is invertible by \(\text{ass:shared-topological-order}\), and the diagonal matrix \(\operatorname{Cov}(\varepsilon^{(a)})=\operatorname{diag}_{j\in V}\Gamma_j[a,a]\) is positive definite by \(\text{ass:disturbance-nondegeneracy}\).  Thus every principal matrix inverted in \(\text{def:modified-cholesky}\) is nonsingular.

For a fixed view \(a\), the row in \(\text{def:modified-cholesky}\) is the unique solution of the normal equations for the linear projection of \(X_{\pi(k)}^{(a)}\) on \(X_{\pi(1:k-1)}^{(a)}\).  Therefore the residuals \(L_\pi^{(a)}X^{(a)}\) are mutually orthogonal within view \(a\), and
\[
R_\pi^{aa}=L_\pi^{(a)}\Sigma^{aa}(L_\pi^{(a)})^{\mathsf T}
\]
is diagonal and positive definite.  Notice also that every \(L_\pi^{(a)}\) is unit triangular in the order \(\pi\), hence invertible.

We first prove necessity and uniqueness.  Suppose a full component-aligned completion with order \(\pi\), coefficient matrices \(\widetilde B^{(a)}\), and disturbances \(\widetilde\varepsilon^{(a)}\) has observed moments \(\mathcal O_S\).  A predecessor variable in view \(a\) is a linear combination of disturbances attached to earlier, hence different, variable labels.  By \(\text{ass:cross-variable-disturbance-orthogonality}\), \(\widetilde\varepsilon_{\pi(k)}^{(a)}\) is orthogonal to every predecessor.  The structural equation consequently gives the normal equations
\[
\operatorname{Cov}\!\left(X_{\pi(k)}^{(a)},X_{\pi(1:k-1)}^{(a)}\right)
=\widetilde B^{(a)}[\pi(k),\pi(1:k-1)]
\operatorname{Cov}\!\left(X_{\pi(1:k-1)}^{(a)}\right).
\]
The covariance on the right is positive definite, so its inverse proves \(\widetilde B^{(a)}=B_\pi^{(a)}\) row by row.  Hence \(L_\pi^{(a)}X^{(a)}=\widetilde\varepsilon^{(a)}\), and component alignment gives
\[
R_\pi^{ab}[i,j]=\operatorname{Cov}\!\left(\widetilde\varepsilon_i^{(a)},\widetilde\varepsilon_j^{(b)}\right)=0,\qquad i\ne j,\quad a,b\in S.
\]
This proves necessity and the asserted uniqueness of \(T_\pi\).

For sufficiency, assume \(\operatorname{offdiag}(R_\pi^{ab})=0\) for all distinct \(a,b\in S\).  The selected joint covariance \(\Sigma^{SS}\) is positive definite because it is the covariance of an invertible linear transform of the stacked disturbances \((\varepsilon_j^{(a)}:j\in V,a\in S)\), whose covariance becomes \(\operatorname{diag}_{j\in V}\Gamma_j[S,S]\succ0\) after grouping coordinates by \(j\).  Congruence therefore gives
\[
\mathscr R_{\pi,S}:=P_S\Sigma^{SS}P_S^{\mathsf T}\succ0.
\]
Within-view off-diagonal entries of \(\mathscr R_{\pi,S}\) vanish by the projection calculation above, and its cross-view, cross-variable entries vanish by the displayed compatibility hypothesis.  After a simultaneous coordinate permutation grouping equal variable labels, it follows that
\[
\mathscr R_{\pi,S}=\operatorname{diag}_{j\in V}\bigl(R_\pi^{ab}[j,j]\bigr)_{a,b\in S}.
\]
Every diagonal block \(\bigl(R_\pi^{ab}[j,j]\bigr)_{a,b\in S}\) is thus positive definite.  For \(a\notin S\), \(R_\pi^{aa}[j,j]>0\) because \(R_\pi^{aa}\succ0\).  Consequently \(\Gamma_{\pi,j}\) in \(\text{def:noise-certificate}\) is, after ordering \(S\) first, the block diagonal matrix
\[
\Gamma_{\pi,j}=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\bigl(R_\pi^{ab}[j,j]\bigr)_{a,b\in S},\ (R_\pi^{aa}[j,j])_{a\in M\setminus S}\right)\succ0.
\]

For each \(j\), take a centered Gaussian vector \((\widetilde\varepsilon_j^{(a)})_{a\in M}\) with covariance \(\Gamma_{\pi,j}\), independently across \(j\), and define
\[
\widetilde X^{(a)}=(L_\pi^{(a)})^{-1}\widetilde\varepsilon^{(a)}.
\]
The coefficient matrices have common order \(\pi\), the coordinate disturbance stacks are independent, and their covariance certificates are positive definite.  Moreover, for every \(a\in M\),
\[
\operatorname{Cov}(\widetilde X^{(a)})
=(L_\pi^{(a)})^{-1}R_\pi^{aa}(L_\pi^{(a)})^{-\mathsf T}=\Sigma^{aa},
\]
while for \(a,b\in S\),
\[
\operatorname{Cov}(\widetilde X^{(a)},\widetilde X^{(b)})
=(L_\pi^{(a)})^{-1}R_\pi^{ab}(L_\pi^{(b)})^{-\mathsf T}=\Sigma^{ab}.
\]
Thus this law is the required full completion of \(\mathcal O_S\).

Finally, under \(\text{ass:centered-gaussian-law}\), the collection of all disturbance stacks is jointly Gaussian because it is a linear transform of \(X\).  By \(\text{ass:cross-variable-disturbance-orthogonality}\), its covariance is block diagonal across \(j\).  Its characteristic function is therefore
\[
\exp\!\left\{-\frac12\sum_{j\in V}t_j^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_jt_j\right\}
=\prod_{j\in V}\exp\!\left\{-\frac12t_j^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_jt_j\right\},
\]
which proves mutual independence of the stacks.  Necessity and sufficiency show that \(\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S)\) indexes all and only the admissible coefficient tuples, and \(\text{def:identified-tuple-set}\) removes precisely their numerical duplicates.  Hence \(\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\) is the complete coefficient equivalence class, rather than a definition of the causal target by an observed functional.

Fix \(\theta\in\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}\).  The formula in \(\text{def:fixed-order-open-parameter-space}\) and positive definiteness of every \(\Gamma_i\) imply \(\Sigma_\theta^{aa}\succ0\).  Hence every principal minor used by \(\text{def:modified-cholesky}\) is strictly positive.  Matrix inversion by the adjugate formula shows that every entry of \(B_\pi^{(a)}\), and then every entry of \(R_\pi^{ab}\), is a rational function of the free coordinates of \(\theta\), with a denominator that is a product of those positive principal minors.  This proves the asserted rationality and also proves that clearing the denominators preserves whether an entry is zero.

Let \(\pi\ne\pi_0\).  Two distinct total orders have a discordant pair, so choose \(u,v\) with \(u\) before \(v\) under \(\pi_0\) and \(v\) before \(u\) under \(\pi\).  In the parameter \(\theta_\pi^{ab}\) of \(\text{def:wrong-order-nonvanishing-witness}\), each of \(\Gamma_u\) and \(\Gamma_v\) is positive definite: after permuting views it is the direct sum of \(\begin{psmallmatrix}1&r\\r&1\end{psmallmatrix}\), whose eigenvalues are \(1-r\) and \(1+r\), and an identity matrix; here \(\lvert r\rvert<1\).  All other \(\Gamma_i\) equal \(I_m\).  The only coefficient \(\beta\) respects \(\pi_0\), so \(\theta_\pi^{ab}\in\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}\).

Variables other than \(u,v\) are independent of this two-coordinate system and hence do not change its regression coefficients.  In each of views \(a,b\), write
\[
X_u=\varepsilon_u,\qquad X_v=\beta\varepsilon_u+\varepsilon_v,\qquad
\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_u)=\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_v)=1.
\]
Since \(v\) precedes \(u\) under \(\pi\), the wrong-order innovations on these coordinates are
\[
\widetilde\varepsilon_v=X_v,\qquad
\widetilde\varepsilon_u=X_u-\frac{\operatorname{Cov}(X_u,X_v)}{\operatorname{Var}(X_v)}X_v
=X_u-\frac{\beta}{1+\beta^2}X_v.
\]
Therefore the \((u,v)\) entry, or its transpose according to the displayed coordinate orientation, is
\[
\operatorname{Cov}\!\left(\widetilde\varepsilon_u^{(a)},\widetilde\varepsilon_v^{(b)}\right)
=\frac{\beta}{1+\beta^2}\left(r_u-r_v\right)\ne0.
\]
The corresponding cleared numerator is nonzero at \(\theta_\pi^{ab}\), whence \(F_\pi^{ab}\) is not the zero polynomial.

The ring of real polynomials is an integral domain, so
\[
Q(\theta):=\prod_{\pi\ne\pi_0}F_\pi^{ab}(\theta)
\]
is a nonzero polynomial.  By \(\text{lem:nonzero-polynomial-null-set}\), its zero set has empty interior and Lebesgue measure zero in the relative Euclidean coordinate space.  The domain \(\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}\) is nonempty and relatively open because strict positive definiteness is open (for example, \(B^{(a)}=0\) and all \(\Gamma_i=I_m\) give a member).  Hence
\[
\mathcal E_{ab,\pi_0}=\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}\cap\{\theta:Q(\theta)=0\}
\]
is proper and relatively Lebesgue null.  Absolute continuity of a parameter law then gives probability zero to this set by the definition of absolute continuity.

For \(\theta\notin\mathcal E_{ab,\pi_0}\), the true order \(\pi_0\) is compatible by \(\text{lem:fixed-order-residual-characterization}\).  For every \(\pi\ne\pi_0\), \(F_\pi^{ab}(\theta)>0\), so at least one off-diagonal residual entry is nonzero and the same lemma excludes \(\pi\).  Thus
\[
\Pi_{\{a,b\}}(\mathcal O_{\{a,b\}})=\{\pi_0\},\qquad
\Theta_{\{a,b\}}(\mathcal O_{\{a,b\}})=\{T_{\pi_0}\}.
\]
Full calibration can only remove orders, and it retains \(\pi_0\); consequently \(\Theta_M(\mathcal O_M)=\{T_{\pi_0}\}\).  The admissible designs all have at least two views, while the preassigned pair already attains full information, so \(\lvert S_{\min}\rvert=2\) by \(\text{def:minimum-calibration}\).  The proof used only order-triangular coefficients and positive-definite coordinate disturbance covariances from \(\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}\); it did not introduce edge minimality or the cited comparator's diversity condition.

The two displayed disturbance vectors are independent and centered Gaussian.  Thus cross-variable disturbance covariances vanish.  The first covariance \(\Gamma_1\) has eigenvalues \(4/5,4/5,7/5\).  For \(\Gamma_2\), the leading principal minors are
\[
1,\qquad 1-\frac1{25}=\frac{24}{25},\qquad
\det(\Gamma_2)=1+2\frac15\frac25\frac15-\frac1{25}-\frac4{25}-\frac1{25}=\frac{99}{125},
\]
so Sylvester's criterion gives \(\Gamma_2\succ0\).  The equations \(X_1^{(a)}=\varepsilon_1^{(a)}\) and \(X_2^{(a)}=X_1^{(a)}+\varepsilon_2^{(a)}\) are linear and respect the order \((1,2)\).  Hence all member properties of \(\mathfrak M_{2,3}^{\mathrm{CA}}\) hold.

Put \(g_i^{ab}=\Gamma_i[a,b]\).  Direct covariance calculation gives, for every pair of views,
\[
\Sigma^{ab}=\begin{pmatrix}g_1^{ab}&g_1^{ab}\\ g_1^{ab}&g_1^{ab}+g_2^{ab}\end{pmatrix},\qquad
\Sigma^{aa}=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
For the true order, \(B_{(1,2)}=\begin{psmallmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{psmallmatrix}\), and multiplication by \(L_{(1,2)}=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&0\\-1&1\end{psmallmatrix}\) on both sides gives
\[
R_{(1,2)}^{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(g_1^{ab},g_2^{ab}).
\]
For the reverse order, the regression coefficient is \(\operatorname{Cov}(X_1,X_2)/\operatorname{Var}(X_2)=1/2\), so
\[
B_{(2,1)}=\begin{pmatrix}0&1/2\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
L_{(2,1)}=\begin{pmatrix}1&-1/2\\0&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Another direct multiplication yields
\[
R_{(2,1)}^{ab}[1,2]=R_{(2,1)}^{ab}[2,1]=\frac12(g_1^{ab}-g_2^{ab}).
\]
For \(H=\{1,2\}\), both cross-covariances equal \(1/5\), so both of the only two orders are compatible.  Their coefficient tuples are exactly the two displayed in the proposition, in every view because all marginal covariance matrices coincide.  For the full pair \(\{1,3\}\), \(g_1^{13}=1/5\) whereas \(g_2^{13}=2/5\); the reverse order is therefore incompatible.  The true order remains compatible, so \(\Theta_M(\mathcal O_M)\) is the asserted singleton by \(\text{lem:fixed-order-residual-characterization}\).  Finally, the reverse-order cleared residual polynomial vanishes for pair \(\{1,2\}\), placing the parameter in \(\mathcal E_{12,(1,2)}\), while the pair \(\{1,3\}\) gives the stated nonzero witness.

All inverses below exist because every \(\Sigma^{aa}\succ0\), so each principal covariance and each Schur complement is positive definite.  Expanding \(\text{def:projected-residual}\) gives, for \(U=U_A\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
C_A^{ab}={}&\Sigma^{ab}[U,U]
-\Sigma^{aa}[U,A]\Sigma^{aa}[A,A]^{-1}\Sigma^{ab}[A,U]\\
&-\Sigma^{ab}[U,A]\Sigma^{bb}[A,A]^{-1}\Sigma^{bb}[A,U]\\
&+\Sigma^{aa}[U,A]\Sigma^{aa}[A,A]^{-1}\Sigma^{ab}[A,A]
\Sigma^{bb}[A,A]^{-1}\Sigma^{bb}[A,U].
\end{aligned}
\]
Every term is indexed only by \(A\), proving the claimed state path independence.

This set-indexed formula is also the result of sequential elimination.  Indeed, let \(r\in U_A\), let \(U'=U_A\setminus\{r\}\), and define
\[
\beta_{A,r}^{(a)}=\frac{C_A^{aa}[U',r]}{C_A^{aa}[r,r]}.
\]
The residual vector \(Z_{A,U'}^{(a)}-\beta_{A,r}^{(a)}Z_{A,r}^{(a)}\) is orthogonal both to \(X_A^{(a)}\) and to \(Z_{A,r}^{(a)}\).  Since
\(\operatorname{span}(X_A^{(a)},X_r^{(a)})=\operatorname{span}(X_A^{(a)},Z_{A,r}^{(a)})\), uniqueness of the orthogonal projection proves
\[
Z_{A\cup\{r\}}^{(a)}=Z_{A,U'}^{(a)}-\beta_{A,r}^{(a)}Z_{A,r}^{(a)}.
\]
Taking cross-covariances gives the Schur update
\[
\begin{aligned}
C_{A\cup\{r\}}^{ab}={}&C_A^{ab}[U',U']
-\beta_{A,r}^{(a)}C_A^{ab}[r,U']
-C_A^{ab}[U',r](\beta_{A,r}^{(b)})^{\mathsf T}\\
&+\beta_{A,r}^{(a)}C_A^{ab}[r,r](\beta_{A,r}^{(b)})^{\mathsf T},
\end{aligned}
\]
again depending only on \(A\cup\{r\}\).

For \(t\in U'\) and distinct \(a,b\in S\), the score in \(\text{def:root-score}\) is exactly
\[
q_{A,r,t}^{ab}
=\operatorname{Cov}\!\left(Z_{A,r}^{(a)},
Z_{A,t}^{(b)}-\frac{C_A^{bb}[t,r]}{C_A^{bb}[r,r]}Z_{A,r}^{(b)}\right)
=\operatorname{Cov}\!\left(Z_{A,r}^{(a)},Z_{A\cup\{r\},t}^{(b)}\right).
\]
We now prove the order criterion by induction on \(\lvert U_A\rvert\).  Fix a suffix order beginning with \(r\).  The within-view Gram--Schmidt residualizer for that suffix factors into the first elimination displayed above followed by an invertible unit-triangular residualizer on \(U'\).  Consequently, for a cross-view block, its final first-to-tail row is
\[
\bigl(q_{A,r,t}^{ab}:t\in U'\bigr)K_b^{\mathsf T},
\]
where \(K_b\) is the invertible tail residualizer.  It vanishes if and only if every \(q_{A,r,t}^{ab}\) vanishes.  Once that row and, by considering the ordered pair \((b,a)\), the corresponding column vanish, the remaining final block is diagonal if and only if the recursively residualized tail block from \(C_{A\cup\{r\}}\) is diagonal.  The one-variable base case is automatic.  Thus a full Gram--Schmidt cross-block is diagonal if and only if the first variable is removable and the same condition holds recursively.  At \(A=\varnothing\), \(\text{lem:fixed-order-residual-characterization}\) converts this algebraic criterion into
\[
\pi\in\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
q_{A_{k-1},\pi(k),t}^{ab}=0
\ \text{for every admissible }k,t,a,b.
\]

Every source-to-sink path adds one new label at each step, hence spells one permutation; the displayed equivalence says that it spells exactly one compatible order.  Conversely every compatible order supplies all its path edges, so the correspondence is bijective.  There are at most \(2^p\) states and at most \(p2^{p-1}\) candidate edges.  For one state, the displayed covariance formula or Schur update, all root scores, and all view-pair checks require a number of exact-real arithmetic operations polynomial in \(p\) and \(m\); storing its observed covariance blocks is polynomial as well.  Memoizing each \(C_A\) once therefore gives the asserted \(O(\operatorname{poly}(p,m)2^p)\) time and memory bounds.

Let the common nonzero coefficient be \(\beta\), and write
\[
v_i=\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_i^{(a)})=\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_i^{(b)})>0,\qquad
c_i=\operatorname{Cov}(\varepsilon_i^{(a)},\varepsilon_i^{(b)}),\quad i=1,2.
\]
Then \(\rho_i^{ab}=c_i/v_i\).  Under the true order,
\[
X_1=\varepsilon_1,\qquad X_2=\beta\varepsilon_1+\varepsilon_2,\qquad
d:=\operatorname{Var}(X_2)=\beta^2v_1+v_2>0.
\]
For the reverse order the regression coefficient of \(X_1\) on \(X_2\) is \(\gamma=\beta v_1/d\).  Hence its two innovations are
\[
\widetilde\varepsilon_2=X_2,\qquad
\widetilde\varepsilon_1=X_1-\gamma X_2=\frac{v_2}{d}\varepsilon_1-\frac{\beta v_1}{d}\varepsilon_2.
\]
Component alignment removes cross-variable covariance, and therefore
\[
\operatorname{Cov}\!\left(\widetilde\varepsilon_1^{(a)},\widetilde\varepsilon_2^{(b)}\right)
=\frac{\beta v_1v_2}{d}\left(\frac{c_1}{v_1}-\frac{c_2}{v_2}\right)
=\frac{\beta v_1v_2}{d}\left(\rho_1^{ab}-\rho_2^{ab}\right).
\]
The transpose-oriented off-diagonal entry has the same zero condition.  Since \(\beta\ne0\), \(v_1,v_2>0\), and \(d>0\), both off-diagonal entries vanish if and only if \(\rho_1^{ab}=\rho_2^{ab}\).  The conclusion now follows from \(\text{lem:fixed-order-residual-characterization}\).

Full calibration imposes every pairwise residual-diagonality condition imposed by \(H\), so
\[
\Theta_M(\mathcal O_M)\subseteq\Theta_H(\mathcal O_H).
\]
Fix a permutation \(\pi\) with \(T_\pi\notin\Theta_M(\mathcal O_M)\).  By \(\text{lem:fixed-order-residual-characterization}\) and \(\text{def:residual-witness}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\pi\notin\Pi_H(\mathcal O_H)
&\Longleftrightarrow \text{ some }\{a,b\}\in\binom H2\text{ has }\operatorname{offdiag}(R_\pi^{ab})\ne0\\
&\Longleftrightarrow \binom H2\cap W_\pi\ne\varnothing.
\end{aligned}
\]
If this intersection condition holds for every coefficient-new \(\pi\), no tuple in \(\Theta_H\setminus\Theta_M\) can remain, proving equality.  Conversely, if it fails for some such \(\pi\), all pairs inside \(H\) have diagonal residual blocks, so \(\pi\in\Pi_H\) and \(T_\pi\in\Theta_H\setminus\Theta_M\); equality fails.  This proves the equivalence while correctly ignoring orders whose numerical tuple is already in \(\Theta_M\).

There are finitely many subsets \(H\).  For each one, \(\text{thm:removed-set-recursion}\) constructs \(\mathcal D_H\) and exactly enumerates its compatible leaves; hashing the resulting \(T_\pi\) values gives \(\Theta_H\).  Testing the displayed intersections certifies sufficiency.  Minimality supplies, for every admissible subset of smaller cardinality, a failed intersection and therefore a surviving coefficient-new tuple.  This finite certificate realizes exactly the optimization in \(\text{def:minimum-calibration}\).  If \(\Theta_M=\{T_{\pi_0}\}\), equality for \(S_{\min}\) identifies that tuple.  Once the common inducing order is known, each \(B_{\pi_0}^{(a)}\) is the unique modified-Cholesky regression functional of the marginal \(\Sigma^{aa}\); hence no unselected cross-view covariance is needed to recover any view's coefficient matrix.

Every \(T\in\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\) has an inducing order \(\pi\).  Each nonzero entry \(B_\pi^{(a)}[j,i]\) points from a predecessor \(i\) to a later vertex \(j\) under \(\pi\), so the union support graph \(G_T\) is acyclic.  Its reachability relation is therefore irreflexive and transitive.  The intersection of these reachability relations over \(T\in\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\) remains irreflexive and transitive, proving that \(\prec_S\) is a strict partial order.

By \(\text{lem:fixed-order-residual-characterization}\), every full component-aligned Gaussian completion of \(\mathcal O_S\) has coefficient tuple in \(\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\), and every tuple in that set is realized by a completion with a positive-definite noise certificate.  For any such completion, its ancestral relations are exactly reachability in the union support graph of its coefficient tuple.  Intersecting over all completions therefore gives exactly the relation in \(\text{def:essential-poset}\).  Numerically duplicate inducing orders have the same tuple and the same graph, so deleting duplicates changes neither this intersection nor its computation.  Since the set is finite, computing each transitive closure and intersecting them is an explicit finite recovery map.

Set \(K=K_{\mathrm{obs}}\) and \(t_\alpha=\sqrt{2\log(2K/\alpha)}\).  By \(\text{ass:centered-gaussian-law}\) and the relevant sourcewise sampling assumption, standardizing an \(n\times d\) data matrix gives a matrix \(G\) whose entries are independent standard normal variables.  Apply \(\text{lem:gaussian-extreme-singular-values}\).  With probability at least \(1-\alpha/K\), its singular values divided by \(\sqrt n\) lie in \([1-\eta,1+\eta]\), where
\[
\eta=\sqrt{d/n}+t_\alpha/\sqrt n.
\]
The imposed condition \(\eta<1\) implies \(n>d\), so the dimension premise of that lemma is satisfied.
For observations with covariance \(\Sigma_0\succ0\), \(\widehat\Sigma=\Sigma_0^{1/2}G^{\mathsf T}G\Sigma_0^{1/2}/n\), and hence, with \(\ell=(1-\eta)^2\) and \(v=(1+\eta)^2\),
\[
\ell\Sigma_0\preceq\widehat\Sigma\preceq v\Sigma_0.
\]
When \(\eta<1\), these inequalities imply
\[
-c\widehat\Sigma\preceq\Sigma_0-\widehat\Sigma\preceq c\widehat\Sigma,\qquad
c=\ell^{-1}-1,
\]
because \(\Sigma_0\preceq\ell^{-1}\widehat\Sigma\), \(\Sigma_0\succeq v^{-1}\widehat\Sigma\), and \(1-v^{-1}\le\ell^{-1}-1\).  Therefore
\[
\|\Sigma_0-\widehat\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le
\bigl((1-\eta)^{-2}-1\bigr)\|\widehat\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
Use this result once with \(d=d_S,n=n_S,\Sigma_0=\Sigma^{SS}\) and once for each \(a\in M\) with \(d=p,n=n_a,\Sigma_0=\Sigma^{aa}\).  The two sampling assumptions provide the required independent and identically distributed rows within each source; no independence between sources is used.  A union bound over the \(K=m+1\) events gives probability at least \(1-\alpha\).  On their intersection, all defining inequalities of \(\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\) hold at \(\mathcal O_S\), and the population covariance matrices are positive definite.  Thus
\[
\Pr\{\mathcal O_S\in\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\}\ge1-\alpha.
\]
The inclusion \(\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\subseteq\widehat\Theta_{S,n}(\alpha)\) now follows directly from the union in \(\text{def:region-inversion}\).

We next prove the deterministic moduli.  Let \(u=d_{\mathrm{obs}}(\mathcal O_S,\mathcal O'_S)\le\lambda_*/2\), fix an order \(\pi\), a view \(a\), and one predecessor set \(P\) in that order.  Write
\[
\beta=\Sigma^{aa}[j,P]\Sigma^{aa}[P,P]^{-1},\qquad
\beta'=\Sigma'^{aa}[j,P]\Sigma'^{aa}[P,P]^{-1}.
\]
Compression does not increase operator norm, so every displayed covariance subblock changes by at most \(u\).  For every unit vector \(x\),
\[
x^{\mathsf T}\Sigma'^{aa}[P,P]x
\ge x^{\mathsf T}\Sigma^{aa}[P,P]x-u
\ge\lambda_*-u\ge\lambda_*/2,
\]
so \(\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma'^{aa}[P,P])\ge\lambda_*/2\).  The resolvent identity gives
\[
\|\Sigma'^{aa}[P,P]^{-1}-\Sigma^{aa}[P,P]^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le \frac{2u}{\lambda_*^2}.
\]
Since \(\|\Sigma^{aa}[j,P]\|_2\le K_*\),
\[
\|\beta'-\beta\|_2
\le \frac{2u}{\lambda_*}+\frac{2K_*u}{\lambda_*^2}
=2u(\lambda_*^{-1}+K_*\lambda_*^{-2}).
\]
Summing the squared row bounds and using operator norm at most Frobenius norm yields
\[
\|B_\pi^{(a)}(\mathcal O'_S)-B_\pi^{(a)}(\mathcal O_S)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L_Bu.
\]

For the perturbed regression row,
\[
\|\beta'\|_2\le\frac{2(K_*+u)}{\lambda_*}\le1+\frac{2K_*}{\lambda_*}.
\]
Thus both the population and perturbed residualizers have operator norm at most
\[
G_*=1+\sqrt p(1+2K_*/\lambda_*).
\]
For an observed pair, abbreviate \(L_a=L_\pi^{(a)}(\mathcal O_S)\) and \(L'_a=L_\pi^{(a)}(\mathcal O'_S)\).  The identity
\[
\begin{aligned}
R_\pi'{}^{ab}-R_\pi^{ab}
={}&L'_a(\Sigma'^{ab}-\Sigma^{ab})L_b'{}^{\mathsf T}
+(L'_a-L_a)\Sigma^{ab}L_b'{}^{\mathsf T}\\
&+L_a\Sigma^{ab}(L'_b-L_b)^{\mathsf T}
\end{aligned}
\]
and submultiplicativity give
\[
\|R_\pi'{}^{ab}-R_\pi^{ab}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le\{G_*^2+2L_BG_*K_*\}u\le L_Ru=\omega_{\mathrm{feas}}(u).
\]

For an ordered vertex pair \(e=(i,j)\), set \(w_e(T)=\max_{a\in M}|B_{ji}^{(a)}|\).  The coefficient bound gives \(|w_e(T')-w_e(T)|\le L_Bu\).  Since \(u\le L_B^{-1}\), population weights are at most \(K_B\) and perturbed weights are at most \(K_B+1\).  For any directed vertex sequence \(g=(v_0,\ldots,v_\ell)\), \(\ell\le p-1\), telescoping the product gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\left|\prod_{h=1}^{\ell}w_{(v_{h-1},v_h)}(T')-\prod_{h=1}^{\ell}w_{(v_{h-1},v_h)}(T)\right|
&\le \ell(K_B+1)^{\ell-1}L_Bu\\
&\le L_{\mathrm{path}}L_Bu=\omega_{\mathrm{path}}(u).
\end{aligned}
\]

If \(\pi\notin\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S)\), \(\text{ass:feasibility-separation}\) and \(\text{def:feasibility-margin}\) supply a selected pair and off-diagonal entry of magnitude at least \(\kappa_{\mathrm{feas}}\).  Entrywise change is bounded by operator-norm change.  Therefore \(\omega_{\mathrm{feas}}(u)\le\kappa_{\mathrm{feas}}/2\) leaves that entry of \(R_\pi'{}^{ab}\) with magnitude at least \(\kappa_{\mathrm{feas}}/2>0\).  Hence
\[
\Pi_S(\mathcal O'_S)\subseteq\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S).
\]

On the coverage event, every \(\mathcal O'_S\in\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\) and \(\mathcal O_S\) lie within their respective radii of the same empirical blocks.  Compression of the selected joint block and the triangle inequality therefore give
\[
d_{\mathrm{obs}}(\mathcal O_S,\mathcal O'_S)\le2\bar r_n(\alpha).
\]
Assume the three displayed small-radius conditions in the theorem.  If \(T'\in\widehat\Theta_{S,n}(\alpha)\), then \(T'=T_\pi(\mathcal O'_S)\) for some \(\mathcal O'_S\in\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\) and \(\pi\in\Pi_S(\mathcal O'_S)\).  The preceding inclusion gives \(\pi\in\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S)\), and the coefficient modulus gives
\[
d_{\mathrm{coef}}\!\left(T',T_\pi(\mathcal O_S)\right)\le2L_B\bar r_n(\alpha).
\]
Conversely, the already proved coverage inclusion puts every population tuple itself in the estimated set.  Both directed Hausdorff bounds now yield
\[
d_{\mathrm H}\!\left(\widehat\Theta_{S,n}(\alpha),\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\right)\le2L_B\bar r_n(\alpha).
\]

It remains to prove exact recovery of the relation.  Since the population tuple set is contained in the estimated set, any ancestry common to the estimated set is common to the population set; thus \(\widehat\prec_{S,n}\subseteq\prec_S\).  Conversely, fix \(i\prec_S j\) and any \(T'=T_\pi(\mathcal O'_S)\) in the estimated set.  Its population counterpart \(T=T_\pi(\mathcal O_S)\) belongs to \(\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\).  By \(\text{ass:path-product-separation}\), some \(i\)-to-\(j\) path in \(G_T\) has weight product at least \(\kappa_{\mathrm{path}}\).  The path modulus leaves the same product for \(T'\) at least \(\kappa_{\mathrm{path}}/2>0\).  Every edge on that path is therefore nonzero in at least one view, so the path belongs to \(G_{T'}\).  This proves \(i\widehat\prec_{S,n}j\), and hence \(\widehat\prec_{S,n}=\prec_S\).

Finally, under the stated limit conditions, the coverage probability \(1-\alpha_n\) tends to one and the assumed vanishing radii make all three small-radius inequalities hold eventually.  The Hausdorff upper bound tends to zero on the coverage event, while the relation is exactly correct there.  This proves Hausdorff consistency and exact essential-poset recovery in probability.

By \(\text{thm:generic-two-view-sufficiency}\), every wrong order \(\pi\ne\pi_0\) has a nonzero off-diagonal residual entry for the selected pair and
\[
\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S)=\{\pi_0\},\qquad \Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)=\{T_{\pi_0}\}.
\]
There are only \(p!-1\) wrong orders.  For each such order the maximum appearing in \(\text{def:feasibility-margin}\) is a strictly positive real number, so their finite minimum is strictly positive.  Under the two sampling assumptions and the stated fixed positive feasibility and path-product margins, all hypotheses of \(\text{thm:covariance-region-inversion}\) apply.  As the sourcewise sample sizes diverge and \(\alpha_n\to0\) with vanishing radii, that theorem gives
\[
d_{\mathrm H}\!\left(\widehat\Theta_{S,n}(\alpha_n),\{T_{\pi_0}\}\right)\xrightarrow{P}0,\qquad
\Pr\{\widehat\prec_{S,n}(\alpha_n)=\prec_S\}\longrightarrow1.
\]
Because the population set is the displayed singleton, \(\prec_S\) is precisely the ancestral relation induced by \(T_{\pi_0}\), completing the specialization.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(d,n\) be positive integers with \(n\ge d\), and let \(G\) be an \(n\times d\) matrix with independent standard normal entries.  For every \(t\ge0\), with probability at least \(1-2\exp(-t^2/2)\),
\[
\sqrt n-\sqrt d-t\le s_{\min}(G)\le s_{\max}(G)\le\sqrt n+\sqrt d+t.
\]

source.locator: Gaussian extreme-singular-value deviation inequality; the sharp Gaussian form is Corollary 5.35 in the author's arXiv survey arXiv:1011.3027
source.verbatim_statement:
Let \(A\) be an \(N\times n\) matrix whose entries are independent standard normal random variables. Then for every \(t\geq 0\), with probability at least \(1-2\exp(-t^2/2)\), one has
\[
\sqrt{N}-\sqrt{n}-t\leq s_{\min}(A)\leq s_{\max}(A)\leq\sqrt{N}+\sqrt{n}+t.
\]

attestation.note: Transcribed from the Gaussian deviation corollary at the cited stable arXiv source; notation was renamed from N,n,A to n,d,G in the core statement.

added_lemmas.justification: This is the sharp finite-dimensional Gaussian singular-value event used to derive the data-dependent operator-norm covariance radii.
added_lemmas.gap: The note uses the published Gaussian matrix bound only as a concentration input; the empirical-radius conversion and simultaneous region inversion are derived here.
added_lemmas.consumer: It supplies simultaneous covariance coverage for the calibration and marginal samples.

added_lemmas.statement: For every positive integer \(d\) and every nonzero real polynomial \(q\) on \(\mathbb R^d\), the zero set \(\{x\in\mathbb R^d:q(x)=0\}\) has \(d\)-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero and empty interior.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
We argue by induction on \(d\).  For \(d=1\), a nonzero polynomial has at most its degree many roots, so its zero set is finite and null.  Suppose the result holds in dimension \(d-1\).  Write \(x=(y,z)\in\mathbb R^{d-1}\times\mathbb R\) and
\[
q(y,z)=\sum_{\ell=0}^{D}c_\ell(y)z^\ell.
\]
Choose \(\ell_0\) such that \(c_{\ell_0}\) is not the zero polynomial.  The exceptional set \(E=\{y:c_\ell(y)=0\text{ for every }\ell\}\) is contained in \(\{y:c_{\ell_0}(y)=0\}\), hence is null by the induction hypothesis.  For \(y\notin E\), the section \(z\mapsto q(y,z)\) is a nonzero univariate polynomial and has finitely many zeros, hence one-dimensional measure zero.  Applying the section formula for Lebesgue measure to the nonnegative indicator of the zero set gives
\[
\lambda_d(\{q=0\}\cap[-R,R]^d)
=\int_{[-R,R]^{d-1}}\lambda_1(\{z\in[-R,R]:q(y,z)=0\})\,dy=0
\]
for every positive integer \(R\): the integrand is zero outside \(E\) and is at most \(2R\) on \(E\).  The zero set is closed because \(q\) is continuous, so the section formula applies, and \(\{q=0\}\) is the countable union of these boxed intersections.  Hence it is null.  A nonempty Euclidean open set contains a ball of positive Lebesgue measure, so a null set has empty interior.  This completes the induction.
added_lemmas.justification: This elementary algebraic-measure lemma converts nonvanishing wrong-order polynomials into a proper null exceptional set.
added_lemmas.gap: It is supporting mathematical infrastructure, not a causal identification claim.
added_lemmas.consumer: It closes the genericity conclusion of the two-view theorem.

added_lemmas.statement: Fix \(\mathcal O_S\) generated by the maintained class and \(T\in\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\).  The inducing-order fiber \(\{\sigma\in\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S):T_\sigma=T\}\) is exactly the set of linear extensions of \(G_T\).  It is connected by swaps of adjacent incomparable vertices.  Consequently, after \(T\) is known, its lexicographically least inducing order and the corresponding positive-definite certificate \(\Gamma_\sigma\) are computable in time polynomial in \(p\) and \(m\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Choose \(\pi\in\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S)\) with \(T_\pi=T\), which exists by \(\text{def:identified-tuple-set}\).  If \(T_\sigma=T\), triangularity of every modified-Cholesky matrix under \(\sigma\) forces each edge \(i\to j\) of \(G_T\) to place \(i\) before \(j\).  Thus \(\sigma\) is a linear extension of \(G_T\).

Conversely, \(\text{lem:fixed-order-residual-characterization}\) supplies a completion with coefficient tuple \(T\), diagonal coordinate-disturbance covariance within every view, and selected cross-variable disturbance covariances equal to zero.  If \(\sigma\) is a linear extension of \(G_T\), every coefficient matrix in \(T\) is strictly lower triangular under \(\sigma\).  In each view, the structural disturbance for a variable is orthogonal to all its \(\sigma\)-predecessors, so the normal equations and positive definiteness of the predecessor covariance show that the order-\(\sigma\) modified-Cholesky regression equals the same coefficient row.  Hence \(T_\sigma=T\).  Its residual cross-blocks are the same diagonal disturbance blocks, so \(\sigma\in\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S)\).

For completeness, two linear extensions of a finite poset are connected by adjacent swaps of incomparable vertices.  Indeed, compare two extensions, move the first vertex of the second extension leftward through the first; every crossed vertex is incomparable with it, since the second extension places the chosen vertex first.  Remove that common first vertex and iterate.  This proves connectivity without invoking an undeclared result.  The lexicographically least extension is obtained greedily by repeatedly selecting the least currently minimal vertex of \(G_T\).  Constructing \(G_T\), performing this topological sort, and evaluating \(\Gamma_\sigma\) from \(\text{def:noise-certificate}\) require only polynomially many matrix-entry inspections and arithmetic operations.  Positive definiteness of the certificate follows from \(\text{lem:fixed-order-residual-characterization}\).
added_lemmas.justification: This is the strongest closed quotient fact: it completely characterizes and canonicalizes the inducing orders of a coefficient tuple once that tuple is known.
added_lemmas.gap: It does not provide the missing child oracle needed to discover every previously unknown tuple fiber with output-sensitive total work.
added_lemmas.consumer: A quotient enumerator can use the lexicographically least linear extension as the canonical inducing order and attach its positive-definite noise certificate.

proposed.statement:
Fix \(p\ge2\), \(m\ge3\), a common order \(\pi_0\), and any preassigned distinct views \(a,b\in M\). On \(\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}\), no edge-minimality condition and no diversity condition from Assumption 2 of HeurtebiseEtAl2026LiMVAM is imposed. For every \(\pi
e\pi_0\), all entries of \(\operatorname{offdiag}(R_\pi^{ab}(	heta))\) are rational functions whose denominators are positive products of principal minors, and the denominator-cleared polynomial \(F_\pi^{ab}\) is not identically zero. More precisely, the witness \(	heta_\pi^{ab}\in\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}\) has a wrong-order residual entry equal, up to transpose orientation, to \( eta(r_u-r_v)/(1+ eta^2)
e0\). Therefore \(\mathcal E_{ab,\pi_0}=\{	heta:\prod_{\pi
e\pi_0}F_\pi^{ab}(	heta)=0\}\) is a proper algebraic subset of \(\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}\). For every \(	heta\in\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}\setminus\mathcal E_{ab,\pi_0}\), \(\Pi_{\{a,b\}}(\mathcal O_{\{a,b\}})=\{\pi_0\}\) and \(\Theta_{\{a,b\}}(\mathcal O_{\{a,b\}})=\Theta_M(\mathcal O_M)=\{T_{\pi_0}\}\). Hence every preassigned view pair is generically sufficient and \(\lvert S_{\min}vert=2\) under the maintained convention \(\lvert Svert\ge2\). The exceptional set has Lebesgue measure zero in the relative Euclidean parameter space and is avoided almost surely by every parameter law absolutely continuous with respect to that Lebesgue measure.
proposed.justification: The theorem shows that two aligned views, chosen before seeing the parameters, generically recover the full-view coefficient tuple and that all failures are confined to an explicit algebraic equality locus.
proposed.gap: HeurtebiseEtAl2026LiMVAM, Section 4.6, Assumption 2 and Theorem 3 obtain full-pair point identification from edgewise cross-view correlation diversity. On a narrower component-aligned Gaussian class, this theorem removes that diversity assumption, fixes an arbitrary pair in advance, and proves generic full-information equivalence by a nonvanishing polynomial for every wrong order; this is a different observation-regime result, not a containment claim for their published class.
proposed.consumer: A coordinate-aligned repeated-sensor study can preassign any two views for paired calibration and retain all remaining views only marginally, with failures localized to a testable finite family of algebraic equalities.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the proved polynomial null-set lemma used by the genericity and almost-sure conclusions.

proposed.statement: Under the Gaussian calibration and marginal sampling conditions, whenever \(\eta_{S,n}<1\) and every \(\eta_{a,n}<1\), the explicit radii in \(\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\) satisfy \(\Pr\{\mathcal O_S\in\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\}\ge1-\alpha\), and on this event \(\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\subseteq\widehat\Theta_{S,n}(\alpha)\). More explicitly, for any positive-definite \(\mathcal O'_S\) with \(u=d_{\mathrm{obs}}(\mathcal O_S,\mathcal O'_S)\le\min\{\lambda_*/2,L_B^{-1}\}\), every order and observed view pair obey \(\|B_\pi^{(a)}(\mathcal O'_S)-B_\pi^{(a)}(\mathcal O_S)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L_Bu\) and \(\|R_\pi^{ab}(\mathcal O'_S)-R_\pi^{ab}(\mathcal O_S)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\omega_{\mathrm{feas}}(u)=L_Ru\); every corresponding directed-path product changes by at most \(\omega_{\mathrm{path}}(u)=L_{\mathrm{path}}L_Bu\). Hence, if \(\omega_{\mathrm{feas}}(u)\le\kappa_{\mathrm{feas}}/2\), then \(\Pi_S(\mathcal O'_S)\subseteq\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S)\). On the coverage event, if \(2\bar r_n(\alpha)\le\min\{\lambda_*/2,L_B^{-1}\}\), \(\omega_{\mathrm{feas}}(2\bar r_n(\alpha))\le\kappa_{\mathrm{feas}}/2\), and \(\omega_{\mathrm{path}}(2\bar r_n(\alpha))\le\kappa_{\mathrm{path}}/2\), then the Hausdorff distance induced by \(d_{\mathrm{coef}}\) from \(\widehat\Theta_{S,n}(\alpha)\) to \(\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\) is at most \(2L_B\bar r_n(\alpha)\), and \(\widehat\prec_{S,n}(\alpha)=\prec_S\). Consequently, if \(\min(n_S,\min_{a\in M}n_a)\to\infty\), the two novel margins are bounded below by \(\kappa_{\mathrm{feas}}>0\) and \(\kappa_{\mathrm{path}}>0\), and \(\alpha_n\to0\) with vanishing radii, then Hausdorff consistency and exact essential-poset recovery hold in probability.
proposed.justification: Set inversion makes uncertainty honest when the population output is non-singleton, while the explicit moduli translate covariance error into branch and ancestral-path stability.
proposed.gap: ChernozhukovHongTamer2007SetInference gives general contour inversion, while GhoshalHonorio2018LinearSEM uses precision-diagonal and nonzero-precision-entry gaps for one recursive graph. Neither source defines the wrong-order residual or common-ancestral path-product margins, nor derives the displayed LiMVAM covariance-to-margin moduli.
proposed.consumer: A future Cam-CAN MEG or fMRI diagnostic analysis can report an uncertainty-aware sensitivity envelope only after checking common-target sampling and failing to reject the component-aligned repeated-sensor mechanism on observed calibration blocks.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the published sharp Gaussian singular-value inequality used by the simultaneous covariance coverage proof.

proposed.statement: Using the quotient-enumeration handle, determine whether every distinct tuple in \(\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\) can be emitted exactly once, together with a canonical inducing order and positive-definite noise certificate, in total \(O(\operatorname{poly}(p,m)2^p+\operatorname{poly}(p,m)N_{\mathrm{out}})\) exact-real arithmetic operations or with polynomial delay, without visiting every compatible source-to-sink path in \(\mathcal D_S\); if this complexity is impossible in the stated oracle model, derive a matching obstruction.
proposed.justification: This is the genuine unresolved step between a compact feasibility DAG and a duplicate-free complete output algorithm.
proposed.gap: GuoPerkovic2021MinimalEffects uses graphical effect signatures, WienobstEtAl2023MECEnumeration outputs graph-distinct DAGs, and WangEtAl2023EquivalenceEnumeration requires a local colored AND--OR congruence not established for global numerical tuples.
proposed.consumer: A complete partial-calibration solver can scale on sparse or degenerate systems where factorially many compatible orders encode only a few coefficient mechanisms.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Wire the proved tuple-fiber characterization into the still-open quotient-enumeration question.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct a child oracle that discovers every coefficient-tuple fiber exactly once with additive subset-state and output cost, or formalize an oracle model and prove a matching lower bound.
open_obligations.obstruction: The fiber lemma canonicalizes inducing orders only after a tuple is known. A removed-set state can be an ideal of many different output support posets, while coefficient equality is determined by completed regression rows rather than by a frozen local edge color. Scanning every ideal for every output costs a product of the subset-state and output counts, and traversing all paths can still be factorial when there is only one output.
open_obligations.attempted: Canonical lexicographic paths, adjacent commuting-swap reduction, hashing completed paths, and reverse search were examined. Lexicographic minimality is only decidable after future parent coefficients are exposed; hashing retains factorial traversal; and reverse search lacks a polynomial-time inverse-child generator for branches accessible only through noncanonical inducing orders. No impossibility theorem is justified because the frozen handle does not specify a sufficiently formal query-oracle model.
open_obligations.partial_result: For every \(T\in\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\), the complete fiber of compatible inducing orders is exactly the set of linear extensions of \(G_T\).  Thus factorial duplication inside a known fiber can be collapsed: the lexicographically least inducing order is obtained by greedy topological sorting, all inducing orders are connected by adjacent incomparable swaps, and \(\Gamma_\pi\succ0\) is then computed in polynomial time.  This does not yet enumerate the previously unknown fibers with additive \(2^p+N_{\mathrm{out}}\) work.
